newsitem.title: USA: CalEnergy drops bid for NYSEG.
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy drops bid for NYSEG.

text.p: Independent power producer CalEnergy Co. Inc. said on Friday it was dropping its attempt to acquire New York State Electric & Gas Corp. due to a lack of support from target company shareholders.

CalEnergy said a $159 million tender offer launched to acquire 9.9 percent of NYSEG shares was undersubscribed. The tender was the first step in its effort to acquire the whole company in a transaction valued at $1.9 billion.
Minimum conditions of the tender offer, which expired at midnight, were not met, CalEnergy said.
"We intend to evaluate our options and explore other potential combinations," CalEnergy said in a news release.
The tender offer was valued at $24.50 per share. NYSEG's stock has been trading above that level, closing Thursday at $25.25.

NYSEG had urged holders not to tender their shares and refused to sit down at the negotiating table, saying that the offer did not reflect the value of the company. CalEnergy launched its effort on July 15, saying it would be willing to pay $27.50 per share in a negotiated transaction.
